summary: Authoritative context recovered read-only. Prioritized repair backlog: P0 — Complete the currently materialized shared-objective, two-project acceptance graph. Evidence: data/workbench/projects.json:448-583 registers the reviewed read-only projects arda-human-reviewed and arda-tool-gate-reviewed; core/projects/tasks/queue.jsonl:40222-40229 materializes recover-context, two project-bound inspections, synthesis, outcome, verification, and joined dependencies under one objective; docs/plans/autonomous-task-completion/04-real-multi-project-execution.md:14-37 says reviewed real projects, shared-objective decomposition, and joined close remain open. Implementation truth: project binding, dependency leaves, provider-backed execution, and disposable-project overlap exist. Configuration truth: the reviewed project contracts are attached with exact roots and clean-tree checks. Live-proof gap: both reviewed projects must be inspected by project-bound read-only workers, independently criticized, and joined under one closure receipt without modifying either worktree. Human-visible behavior: one objective reports evidence for both real projects and closes only when both contracts pass. Smallest authoritative surface: existing data/workbench/projects.json contracts, Engine/Workbench run graph, canonical queue ledger, and objective join logic; create no new queue or coordinator. P1 — Prove one same-objective deferred or recurring wake across restart. Evidence: docs/plans/autonomous-task-completion/README.md:34 and docs/plans/autonomous-task-completion/02-installed-scheduling-restart.md:14-45 identify this as the remaining scheduling gate. Implementation truth: timer execution, pause and terminal suppression, forced restart, verification/review continuation, and unattended correction are proven. Configuration truth: the installed user-systemd scheduler and binary/source identity must be current. Live-proof gap: a canonical deferred or recurring schedule must wake after restart and reach terminal acceptance exactly once. Human-visible behavior: work resumes at its displayed wake time without another instruction and cannot wake after pause, cancellation, or closure. Smallest authoritative surface: core/projects/tasks/schedules.jsonl, the installed timer consumer, RunStore checkpoints, and existing continuation policy. P2 — Bind live Vairë context use and obtain operator acceptance. Evidence: docs/plans/autonomous-task-completion/README.md:37,64-78 and docs/plans/autonomous-task-completion/05-vaire-operator-acceptance.md:14-49 say terminal outcome memory exists but pre-execution context-use, new-session recovery, and the burden verdict remain open. Implementation truth: durable Mnemosyne terminal outcome binding exists. Configuration truth: authorized personal/business/system retrieval scopes must be selected explicitly. Live-proof gap: record a Vairë context-use receipt before execution, recover it in a new Hermes session, and obtain the operator verdict. Human-visible behavior: the operator can return later and receive accurate prior context, current state, and next action without restating the objective. Smallest authoritative surface: Vairë retrieval/context-use receipts, existing Hermes objective projection, and terminal outcome binding. P3 — Close the genuine messaging-platform objective-control gate. Evidence: docs/plans/autonomous-task-completion/01-hermes-objective-control.md:14-55 reports installed loopback control acceptance but leaves a real external-platform receipt open. Implementation truth: intake, projection reads, pause/resume, reprioritization, revision, approval, cancellation, and terminal suppression exist. Configuration truth: a gateway-connected messaging route must be admitted and authenticated. Live-proof gap: exercise the controls through one genuine delivered message and bind the command receipt to canonical records. Human-visible behavior: conversational status and controls operate without IDs or ledger editing. Smallest authoritative surface: Hermes bridge consumption of OperatorProjection plus existing Aulë mutation owners. P4 — Repair active status drift before using documentation as planning evidence. Evidence: ARDA_SYSTEM_STATUS_REPORT.md:47 already states full verify/review/close proof, contradicting docs/audits/2026-08-26-operator-vision-repair-backlog.md:47,162-168, which says the report omits it; ARDA_SYSTEM_STATUS_REPORT.md:48 says the registry has three proof/demo contracts, while data/workbench/projects.json:198-583 contains acceptance, real-project, and reviewed-project contracts beyond the first three. Implementation truth: these are documentation defects, not missing executor features. Configuration truth: the live registry currently contains nine contracts, including two reviewed read-only real-project contracts. Live-proof gap: registry presence does not itself prove successful shared-objective joined execution. Human-visible behavior: status surfaces distinguish implemented, configured/registered, and live-proven capability without stale counts or contradictory maturity claims. Smallest authoritative surface: ARDA_SYSTEM_STATUS_REPORT.md and docs/audits/2026-08-26-operator-vision-repair-backlog.md, derived from the structured program and canonical registry; generated queue projections remain untouched. P5 — After P0-P4, run the single program acceptance objective defined at docs/plans/autonomous-task-completion/README.md:64-78, then proceed to provider convergence, connected-project fabric, daily improvement, external assimilation, and whole-system acceptance in docs/plans/ARDA_WHOLE_SYSTEM_COMPLETION_PROGRAM.md:49-97. Milestone 3 needs no repair: docs/plans/autonomous-task-completion/03-live-critic-revision.md:14-40 records completed live rejection, durable revision, corrected execution, and independent acceptance. No project files were modified and the verifier-owned cargo test was intentionally not run.
